Cycle 75: code-review (medium) of app/egx_scan_dispatch.py found one real concurrency defect — dispatch_scan read the pre-claim attempt_count via a separate non-atomic get_job() call, then required the post-claim_job() attempt_count to equal exactly previous_count+1; claim_job() itself is a correct atomic CAS (UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('PENDING','FAILED') OR stale RUNNING) that tolerates a concurrent worker claiming/releasing the same job between the two reads, so a second worker's legitimately atomic claim could land on a higher attempt_count and spuriously raise RuntimeError('invalid claimed scan attempt'), aborting the dispatch cycle despite a correctly claimed job. Fixed by removing the previous_count baseline and comparison entirely: valid_scheduler_attempt() already enforces attempt_count is a positive int, and the existing guarded_key/expected_attempt compare-and-swap on mark_succeeded/mark_failed already protects downstream stages, so no correctness was lost. Added tests/test_egx_scan_dispatch.py::test_concurrent_reclaim_does_not_crash_on_attempt_count_gap simulating a claim_job() CAS landing on attempt_count=3 after a pre-claim read of 0, confirming the dispatcher now completes successfully instead of raising. Cycle 75 second slice: code-review (medium) of app/ui/operational.py found one real bug and one real cross-module consistency gap, both fixed. (1) render_operational's WATCH trade-plan block used `if item['status']=='WATCH' and plan:` (truthiness), so a hash-consistent receipt tampered to `trade_plan={}` (empty dict, falsy) skipped the block entirely instead of showing the existing 'UNKNOWN (incomplete receipt)' fallback — silently presenting a WATCH symbol with zero plan information and zero warning, contradicting the adjacent comment's own invariant. Fixed by checking `plan is not None` instead of truthiness (None still legitimately skips the block; any other value, including {} or a wrong type, now reaches the existing isinstance/completeness check and falls through to the UNKNOWN fallback). New parametrized case `trade_plan={}` added to tests/test_operational_ui.py::test_incomplete_receipt_renders_unknown_not_partial. (2) The operator-configured-path symlink safety check (`any(part.is_symlink() for part in (path, *path.parents))`) existed as three independent copies: app/egx_scan_history.py's _symlinked (already deduped internally in cycle 74), a fresh inline copy added in app/ui/operational.py, and a divergent, narrower copy in app/main.py's shadow() endpoint that checked only `directory.parents`, never `directory` itself. Extracted one shared app/path_safety.symlinked() helper and wired all three call sites to it (egx_scan_history.py keeps its `_symlinked` name as a local alias for zero-diff at its two call sites). Verified main.py's narrower check was not independently exploitable — app/ui/shadow.py's load_shadow_watchlist already checks `directory.is_symlink()` itself as defense-in-depth, confirmed by temporarily stashing the fix and re-running an added integration-level test, which passed even pre-fix (so that test was dropped as non-discriminating, consistent with test-honesty: do not claim a test proves a fix it does not exercise). Added tests/test_path_safety.py instead, a direct unit test of the shared helper proving it rejects both a symlinked target itself and a symlinked parent, and accepts a plain path — this does discriminate main.py's prior narrower check. The main.py change remains a legitimate defense-in-depth/consistency fix, not a claimed live-vulnerability fix.
